newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities slightly firmer.

text.p: Implied volatilities for shorter-dated U.S. Treasury bond options were slightly firmer in light pre-holiday trading as the underlying market tumbled on stronger than expected economic data, dealers said.
Although bidding was far from aggressive, a slide of more than a full point in March futures prompted offers to back off in an already cautious, thin-volume environment, they said.

Implied volatilities for February and March T-bond futures options were up 0.1-0.2 point to 9.6 and 10.1 percent in late morning trade. Further-out months were steadier on thin volume, with June staying flat at about 9.95 percent.
Traders noted a distinct lack of selling pressure in volatilities in the past few days, despite a relatively quiet bond market and time-decay concerns over the New Year's Day holiday.
"It has been holding in well," said a T-bond trader for a U.S. bank affiliate at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT). "But it's been on the low end (of historical ranges)."

Among the few large deals in the CBOT pit today, a British firm was seen buying March 110/112 put spreads in a one-by-two ratio, 1,000 legs. Trading at CBOT was to end early at 1210 CST/1810 GMT today and be shut all day on Wednesday.
Implied volatilities for Eurodollar options were also steady to firmer in slow trade, with virtually no large trades, dealers said.
"It's been busier than the last few days, but there hasn't really been a great deal of activity," a brokerage firm trader said.
Eurodollar trading at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange was to close at 1200 CST/1800 GMT.
Implied volatilities for March and June Eurodollar futures options were up about 0.1 point at about 9.4 and 13.8 percent respectively.

Earlier in the day, fixed income markets slid on news that November U.S. new single-family home sales jumped 14.2 percent to an annualized rate of 772,000 units, well above forecasts for a 731,000 unit rate.

Traders said the market was awaiting further economic data due out in the coming weeks. The December National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index is due on Thursday, and the December employment report is due out on January 10.
"Thursday we have the NAPM, plus it's the beginning of the year, so I would imagine a lot of proprietary traders would be back," the CBOT trader said.
